selectedOriginals.caption: The Apollo Theater at 253 West 125th Street between Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Boulevard and Frederick Douglass Boulevard in the Harlem neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City[ is a music hall and a noted venue for African-American performers. The theater was built in 1913-14 as Hurtig & Seamon's New Burlesque Theater, and was designed by George Keister in the neo-Classical style. It became the Apollo in 1934, when it was opened to black patrons – previously it has been a whites-only venue.
selectedOriginals.inspection: 2013 full native original individually inspected. Four-bay white glazed terracotta facade above remodeled ground floor, five tall pilasters/three fluted Ionic central and two paneled end piers, paired window/transom tiers, shield/fluted spandrels and Greek fret under deep modillion cornice, balustered parapet. Western half has projecting marquee with pale panels/blue bands and APOLLO cap on its short side; perpendicular blade is supported by open black steel trestle above roof. No adjacent Banana Republic/GameStop.
